name: fortinet-fortiaigate
label: Fortinet FortiAIGate
description: Fortinet FortiAIGate is an inline AI gateway that brokers and guards access to large language model providers. This connector manages the gateway's virtual keys - the data-plane API keys that client applications present to the gateway's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Operations cover listing and inspecting virtual keys, creating keys (the gateway returns the key secret exactly once), rotating a key in place (invalidating the old secret and issuing a new one), revoking keys, setting key expiry and rate limits, and validating a key against the data-plane models endpoint. Built for the FortiAIGate 8.x management API (session cookie plus per-mutation CSRF, admin console JSON API). Version 1.1 adds governed AI usage: chat completions through the data plane, guardrail testing, policy and provider visibility, workspace budgets and audit logs. Version 1.4 works with a workspace login as well as an organization administrator: the connector reads the login's role and, for a workspace admin or member, manages that workspace's keys, guardrails, policies, detectors and logs. Version 1.6 adds scheduled data ingestion: the prebuilt Data Ingestion playbooks read the requests FortiAIGate blocked (with the prompt, the detectors that fired and the sending virtual key) and create one FortiSOAR alert per blocked request. Version 1.7 merges the 1.6.1 - 1.6.13 security hardening (URL-encoded ids, Vault path checks, revoke-and-rotate-peers on guardrail block, traffic-log replay guard, fail-closed key resolution, dedup / short-circuit on already-revoked, completion marker written only after remediation) with scheduled ingestion.

fields.name: server
fields.title: Server URL
fields.description: Base URL of the FortiAIGate management console. The connector logs in with the credentials below, then calls the JSON API under /api/v1.

fields.name: username
fields.title: Username
fields.description: Username of a FortiAIGate account: an organization administrator, or a workspace admin or member. The connector detects which: an organization administrator manages every workspace (the /api/v1/admin API); any other login manages its own workspace (/api/v1/workspaces/<id>).

fields.name: workspace
fields.title: Workspace
fields.description: (Optional) For a workspace login only: the name or id of the workspace the connector acts in. Leave it blank when the account is a member of one workspace; it is then used automatically. An organization administrator ignores it.

fields.name: verify_ssl
fields.title: Verify SSL
fields.description: Specifies whether the SSL certificate of the FortiAIGate server is to be verified. The workshop/lab gateway serves a self-signed certificate, so leave this unchecked there.

fields.name: data_plane_base
fields.title: Data Plane Base URL
fields.description: Optional base URL used for validating API keys against the data plane. Defaults to the same origin as the management Server URL. Only set this when the data plane is published at a different address.

fields.name: timeout
fields.title: Request Timeout (seconds)
fields.description: Per-request timeout in seconds applied to every management and data-plane HTTP call.

operations.title: List Workspaces
operations.description: List the FortiAIGate workspaces: every workspace for an organization administrator, the login's own workspaces otherwise. Virtual keys are created inside a workspace, so use this to resolve a workspace_id for the Create Virtual Key operation.

operations.title: List Virtual Keys
operations.description: List the virtual keys on the FortiAIGate gateway. Optionally filter by workspace or status. Each record includes the key id, name, active status, expiry (expiresAt), usage (lastUsedAt, spend) and the secret preview - the secret itself is never returned by the management API.

parameters.title: Workspace ID
parameters.name: workspace_id
parameters.tooltip: (Optional) Only list virtual keys in this workspace.
parameters.description: (Optional) Only list virtual keys in this workspace.

parameters.title: Status
parameters.name: status
parameters.description: (Optional) Only list virtual keys with this status.

operations.title: List Expiring Virtual Keys
operations.description: List the virtual keys that expire within a number of days, soonest first, and (by default) those that already have. A key with no expiry, and a revoked or suspended key, is never listed. Feed the key ids to a renewal flow.

parameters.title: Workspace ID
parameters.name: workspace_id
parameters.tooltip: (Optional) Only list virtual keys in this workspace.
parameters.description: (Optional) Only keys in this workspace. Empty lists every key the login can see.

parameters.title: Within (Days)
parameters.name: within_days
parameters.description: (Optional) List keys that expire within this many days from now. Default 7; 0 lists only expired keys.

parameters.title: Include Expired
parameters.name: include_expired
parameters.description: Also list keys that have already expired. Default on.

operations.title: Get Virtual Key
operations.description: Retrieve a single virtual key record by its id.

parameters.title: Key ID
parameters.name: key_id
parameters.tooltip: UUID of the virtual key, as returned by List Virtual Keys.
parameters.description: UUID of the virtual key to retrieve.

operations.title: Create Virtual Key
operations.description: Create a new virtual key in a workspace. FortiAIGate returns the key secret (secretKey) exactly once, in the response to this operation - it is never readable again, so store it immediately (for example in HashiCorp Vault).

parameters.title: Workspace ID
parameters.name: workspace_id
parameters.description: Workspace in which to create the key. Resolve with List Workspaces. Required for an organization administrator; a workspace login defaults to its workspace.

parameters.title: Key Name
parameters.name: key_name
parameters.description: Display name of the new virtual key.

parameters.title: Expires At
parameters.name: expires_at
parameters.description: (Optional) Expiry timestamp in ISO 8601. Leave empty for a key that does not expire.

parameters.title: Expires In (Days)
parameters.name: expires_in_days
parameters.description: (Optional) Expire the key this many days from now. Ignored when Expires At is set.

parameters.title: TPM
parameters.name: tpm
parameters.description: (Optional) Tokens-per-minute limit for the new key.

parameters.title: RPM
parameters.name: rpm
parameters.description: (Optional) Requests-per-minute limit for the new key.

parameters.title: Providers
parameters.name: provider_ids
parameters.description: (Optional) AI provider ids the key may use, comma-separated; the key gets every model of each. FortiAIGate 8.0.2 requires model access, so a key created without it is refused.

operations.title: Update Virtual Key
operations.description: Update the expiry or the TPM/RPM limits of a virtual key. The management API replaces the whole key configuration on update, so this operation first reads the current record and merges in only the fields you supply - everything else is preserved.

parameters.title: Key ID
parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: UUID of the virtual key to update.

parameters.title: Expires At
parameters.name: expires_at
parameters.description: (Optional) New expiry timestamp in ISO 8601. Leave empty to keep the current value.

parameters.title: TPM
parameters.name: tpm
parameters.description: (Optional) New tokens-per-minute limit. Leave empty to keep the current value.

parameters.title: RPM
parameters.name: rpm
parameters.description: (Optional) New requests-per-minute limit. Leave empty to keep the current value.

parameters.title: Policy IDs
parameters.name: policy_ids
parameters.description: (Optional) Comma-separated policy ids to attach to the key. Replaces the current attached policy list; policies the organization forces onto the workspace always stay attached.

operations.title: Rotate Virtual Key
operations.description: Rotate a virtual key in place: FortiAIGate invalidates the old secret and issues a new one for the same key id. Pass either the key (id or name), or the key secret itself (api_key); the connector derives the id from the secret. The response carries the new secret as secretKey - store it immediately (for example by writing it to HashiCorp Vault), as it is not readable again.

parameters.title: Key ID
parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: (Optional) UUID of the virtual key to rotate. Leave empty when passing the key secret instead.

parameters.title: API Key
parameters.name: api_key
parameters.description: (Optional) The virtual key secret itself; the connector derives the key id from it. Starts with 'faig_'.

operations.title: Renew Virtual Key
operations.description: Give a virtual key a new secret, keeping its id, name, limits, policies and model access. The expiry moves to Extend By (Days) from now when it would come sooner - so a key renewed ahead of its expiry does not expire anyway days later - and is never shortened. An expired key is extended first, because FortiAIGate only rotates an active key. A key with no expiry is only rotated. A revoked or suspended key is refused. If the rotate fails after the extend, the original expiry is put back (an expired key is revoked if that also fails), so the old secret never stays working. The new secret is returned as secretKey and is shown only once - store it immediately, for example in HashiCorp Vault.

parameters.title: Key ID
parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: (Optional) The virtual key to renew, by name or id. Leave empty when passing the key secret instead.

parameters.title: API Key
parameters.name: api_key
parameters.description: (Optional) The virtual key secret itself; the connector derives the key id from it. Starts with 'faig_'.

parameters.title: Extend By (Days)
parameters.name: expires_in_days
parameters.description: (Optional) New expiry this many days from now, applied when the key would expire sooner. Default 30, at most 3650.

operations.title: Revoke Virtual Key
operations.description: Revoke a virtual key. After revocation the key secret stops working on the data plane; the record remains visible with status 'revoked'.

parameters.title: Key ID
parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: UUID of the virtual key to revoke.

parameters.title: Reason
parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: (Optional) Why the key is being revoked; FortiAIGate records it with the revocation. Defaults to 'Revoked from FortiSOAR'.

operations.title: Check API Key
operations.description: Validate a virtual key secret against the data plane by calling the OpenAI-compatible models endpoint with it. Returns valid=true with the model count on success (HTTP 200), or valid=false with the HTTP status for a rejected key (401/403 for expired, revoked or suspended keys). This is the preferred 'is this key expired?' detector in rotation playbooks.

parameters.title: API Key
parameters.name: api_key
parameters.description: The virtual key secret to validate (starts with 'faig_').

operations.title: Chat Completion
operations.description: Run one OpenAI-compatible chat completion through the FortiAIGate data plane using a virtual key. Guardrails and policies attached to the key's workspace are enforced by the gateway, so playbook AI steps inherit its scanning and blocking. Returns the OpenAI-format completion: the assistant text is at choices[0].message.content, and a blocked prompt comes back with finish_reason content_filter.

parameters.title: API Key
parameters.name: api_key
parameters.description: The virtual key secret to authenticate with (starts with 'faig_').

parameters.title: Model
parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Model to complete with, e.g. openai-gpt-4.1-mini. Use List Models on the data plane (Check API Key also returns the count) or the provider catalog naming.

parameters.title: Messages (JSON)
parameters.name: messages
parameters.description: Chat messages as a JSON list, e.g. [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize this alert."}]

parameters.title: Max Tokens
parameters.name: max_tokens
parameters.description: (Optional) Maximum completion tokens.

parameters.title: Temperature
parameters.name: temperature
parameters.description: (Optional) Sampling temperature, 0.0 to 2.0.

operations.title: Test Guardrail
operations.description: Scan arbitrary text through the gateway's guardrail scanner. No provider or upstream model is involved: the operation answers 'would these detectors fire?'. Pass detector ids directly, or a guardrail id to reuse its detectors and character-deny setting. Use it to triage prompts and model outputs inside playbooks.

parameters.title: Input Text
parameters.name: input_text
parameters.description: The text to scan (a prompt, a model response, an email body).

parameters.title: Detector IDs
parameters.name: detector_ids
parameters.description: (Optional) Comma-separated detector ids to run.

parameters.title: Guardrail ID
parameters.name: guardrail_id
parameters.description: (Optional) Test with this guardrail's detectors and deny-suspicious-characters setting.

parameters.title: Deny Suspicious Characters
parameters.name: deny_suspicious_characters
parameters.description: (Optional) Deny Suspicious Characters

operations.title: List Policies
operations.description: List the organization's AI policies with their guardrail assignments, provider access and status. With workspace_id, also includes that workspace's own policies.

parameters.title: Workspace ID
parameters.name: workspace_id
parameters.description: (Optional) Also list this workspace's own policies.

operations.title: Get Policy
operations.description: Retrieve a single policy by id, including input and output guardrail ids, provider access and any pending change.

parameters.title: Policy ID
parameters.name: policy_id
parameters.description: UUID of the policy.

operations.title: List Guardrails
operations.description: List the organization's guardrails (named detector sets) with their detector ids and the number of policies using each.

operations.title: Get Guardrail
operations.description: Retrieve a single guardrail by id, including its detector ids and deny-suspicious-characters setting.

parameters.title: Guardrail ID
parameters.name: guardrail_id
parameters.description: UUID of the guardrail.

operations.title: List AI Providers
operations.description: List the AI providers the gateway can reach, with their platform, base URL, model counts and configured key counts. Useful when keys fail because an upstream provider is down or out of keys. Needs an organization administrator.

operations.title: Get Workspace Budget
operations.description: Get a workspace's spend against its budget and the budget cycle.

parameters.title: Workspace ID
parameters.name: workspace_id
parameters.description: UUID of the workspace. Resolve with List Workspaces. Required for an organization administrator; a workspace login defaults to its workspace.

operations.title: List Audit Logs
operations.description: List the gateway's administration audit events (logins, key and policy changes), newest first. Returns the items, the total on the first page, and nextCursor (pass it back as Cursor for the next page).

parameters.title: Cursor
parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: (Optional) The nextCursor of the previous page. Leave empty for the first page.

parameters.title: Range
parameters.name: range
parameters.description: (Optional) The period to list: the last 24 hours, 7 days, month, or all. Default all.

parameters.title: Limit
parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: (Optional) Page size, default 25.

operations.title: Get Traffic Log
operations.description: Fetch one traffic-log record by its request id (uuid). Returns the virtual key that sent the request, the gateway's verdict and the detectors that fired, so the revocation playbook can confirm a guardrail block before acting.

parameters.title: Request Id
parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: The traffic log's uuid (the FortiAIGate request id).

operations.title: Get Audit Log Filter Options
operations.description: The filter dimensions available for the audit log (users, workspaces, roles, actions), for building dashboards and picklists.

operations.title: Get Blocked Traffic
operations.description: Read the requests FortiAIGate blocked, newest first. Each record has the prompt, the response if any, the detectors that fired (name, type, side, details), the reason, the sending virtual key (name, prefix, id, status) and the key's owner. Since (the last pull time, epoch milliseconds or an ISO 8601 datetime) with an optional Until reads a custom window; without Since, Range counts back from now. The scheduled ingestion uses this to create alerts.

parameters.title: Since
parameters.name: since
parameters.description: (Optional) Only blocked requests at or after this time: epoch milliseconds or an ISO 8601 datetime such as 2026-10-15T10:00:00Z. A poller passes its last pull time here. Blank reads the Range instead.

parameters.title: Until
parameters.name: until
parameters.description: (Optional) The end of the window that starts at Since: epoch milliseconds or an ISO 8601 datetime. Default now. Needs Since.

parameters.title: Range
parameters.name: range
parameters.description: (Optional) Used when Since is blank: the last 24 hours, 7 days, month, or all. Default 24h.

parameters.title: Max Items
parameters.name: max_items
parameters.description: (Optional) Most blocked requests to read, newest first. Default 100. Each one costs a request to FortiAIGate.

parameters.title: Workspace ID
parameters.name: workspace_id
parameters.description: (Optional) Only blocked requests in this workspace. Leave empty for every workspace the login can see.

operations.title: List My Workspaces
operations.description: List the workspaces the configured administrator account is a member of. Create Virtual Key requires the key owner to be a member of the target workspace, so use this to pick a workspace id for key creation.

operations.title: Get Workspace Options
operations.description: Populates workspace dropdowns with plain names: every workspace for an organization administrator, the login's own workspaces otherwise. The action resolves the picked name to the workspace id.

operations.title: Get Virtual Key Options
operations.description: Populates virtual key dropdowns with plain key names (renewed keys keep their name; when two keys share a name the one active key is used). The action resolves the picked name to the key id.

operations.title: Get Policy Options
operations.description: Populates policy dropdowns with plain policy names. The action resolves the picked name to the policy id.

operations.title: Get Guardrail Options
operations.description: Populates guardrail dropdowns with plain guardrail names. The action resolves the picked name to the guardrail id.

operations.title: Get Detector Options
operations.description: Populates detector dropdowns with plain detector names: the built-in detectors, then the custom detectors. The action resolves the picked name to the detector id.

operations.title: Get Model Options
operations.description: Populates the chat completion model dropdown with the public model names of the model groups the login can use (the identifiers the completions endpoint accepts). Empty when the login has no model group; type the model name then.

operations.title: Execute API Request
operations.description: Calls any FortiAIGate management API endpoint with the configured login. A full URL is refused so the credentials only ever go to the configured server.

parameters.title: Endpoint
parameters.name: endpoint
parameters.description: Path on the configured FortiAIGate server, for example /api/v1/admin/workspaces.

parameters.title: Method
parameters.name: method
parameters.description: HTTP method. Defaults to GET.

parameters.title: Query Parameters
parameters.name: query_params
parameters.description: (Optional) JSON object of query string parameters.

parameters.title: Request Body
parameters.name: request_body
parameters.description: (Optional) JSON object sent with POST, PUT and PATCH.
